story.name: トウキョウ ひとりぐらし
story.title: Mount Fuji on the Wall
story.line: ブーケが はじめて せんとうに いきます
story.ja: 夕方がやっと涼しくなったある木曜、仕事帰りのブーケをアリゲッティが銭湯にさそう。男湯と女湯は別。木の札の靴箱、初めての人はアリゲッティのおごり。「まず体を洗ってから湯船へ」。壁いっぱいに富士山の絵。お湯は熱くて「スープじゃないの？」。でもゆっくり入ると、区役所の用紙もごみの日も全部とけていく。向かいのおばあさんの「何年も通ってる人みたい」は、最高のほめ言葉。最後は腰に手をあててコーヒー牛乳。「毎週木曜ね」と約束し、小雨の中、紺色の傘にふたりで入って帰る。

segments.en: A few days later, the evenings were finally cooler. The cicadas had gone quiet, and the crickets had taken over.
One Thursday, Rosie came home late, stiff from a long day at her desk. Gayle was on the stairs, holding a little plastic basket.
Perfect timing! I'm going to the bathhouse. Why don't you come along? Nothing fixes a long day like a hot bath. Bring a towel.
A public bath? With other people? Um. I've never done that. Is it, like, everybody together?
Men on one side, women on the other. Don't worry, I'll show you everything. And if you hate it, you never have to go again.
The bathhouse was three streets away, on a corner. It had a tall chimney, a blue cloth curtain over the door, and a sign Rosie couldn't read yet.
Inside, they put their shoes in little lockers with wooden keys, and Gayle paid for both of them before Rosie could find her wallet.
My treat. You're a first-timer, and first-timers don't pay. That's my rule, not theirs.
In the changing room, a few older ladies were drying their hair. One of them smiled at Rosie, the kind of smile that says, oh, a new one.
Rosie was nervous. But nobody was looking at anybody. Everyone was just there to get clean and warm, and to talk about their grandchildren.
Rule number one. You wash first, sitting on a stool. Then you get in. The bath is for soaking, not for washing.
So they sat on low plastic stools in front of little mirrors and washed. Then Rosie stood up, turned around, and saw the wall.
It was covered with a huge painting of Mount Fuji. Blue sky, snow on top, and a blue lake at the bottom.
Whoa. Gayle. There's a mountain. There's a whole mountain on the wall.
Isn't it lovely? A lot of the old bathhouses have one. Somebody painted it by hand, and every few years, they touch it up.
Then Rosie put one foot in the water, and pulled it right back out.
Oh my gosh, it's so hot! How is anybody sitting in this? Are you sure this isn't soup?
Take it slow. One foot, then the other. Then sit, and don't move. Believe me, in a minute, you won't want to get out.
Rosie went in very slowly. Then she sat down, up to her shoulders, and let out a long breath.
The heat went into her shoulders, her back, and her tired feet. The ward office forms, the trash days, all of it just floated away.
Okay. I take it back. This is the best thing that's ever happened to me. I'm never getting out. I live here now.
An old lady across the bath laughed and said something to Gayle in Japanese. Gayle laughed too.
Wait, what did she say? Was it about me?
She said you look like you've been coming here for years. That's a compliment, dear. A big one.
They soaked until their faces were pink. Then they got dressed, and Gayle bought two little glass bottles of coffee milk from a fridge by the door.
Now, this is important. You drink it standing up, with one hand on your hip. Like this. Don't ask me why. It's just how it's done.
So they stood side by side, each with one hand on her hip, and drank their coffee milk all at once. It was sweet and cold and perfect.
Oh, that hits the spot. Gayle, I'm serious. Can we do this every Thursday?
Every Thursday. It's a date. But next time, you bring your own towel.
Outside, it had started to drizzle. Rosie opened the big navy umbrella over both of them, and they walked home slowly, warm all the way through.
You know, I keep meaning to give this back to you. And then it rains every single time.
Then it's doing its job, isn't it? Keep it a little longer.
That night, Rosie slept better than ever. She dreamed she was floating on a warm blue lake, at the foot of a very big mountain.

ph.trap: 沿って来る ではなく、ついて来る、同行する
わたしのごほうび ではなく「ここは払うよ」
first time の人＝初心者、初めて来た人
ゆっくり取る ではなく、あせらず少しずつ
返品する ではなく、言ったことを撤回する
場所に当たる ではなく、まさにほしかった味
デート ではなく、約束成立の決まり文句

predict.ask: さいごの はなしで、ブーケは かさを どうする？
choices: She finally gives it back, with a gift, and Gayle hands it right back to her.
She leaves it on a train and searches all over Tokyo for it.
A strong wind blows it into the river.
predict.ja: やっと引っ越しのあいさつの品を持って返しに行くが、アリゲッティは傘をそのままくれる。
